title: Ptolemy Converse: Equality Implies Cyclic Order
description: Proves the converse direction of Ptolemy's concyclicity characterization: for four distinct unit-circle points, Ptolemy equality implies the points are in CCW or CW cyclic order. Combined with PtolemysTheoremOQ01.lean, this yields the full biconditional: Ptolemy equality ↔ CCW or CW order. The proof uses the exponential difference factorization to derive a sine ratio identity, then an 8-case sign analysis to recover the angle ordering.

overview.historicalContext:
Ptolemy of Alexandria (c. 100-170 CE) proved the theorem bearing his name in the *Almagest* (c. 150 CE), the foundational treatise of Greek mathematical astronomy. In the form |AC||BD| = |AB||CD| + |BC||DA|, it relates the diagonals and sides of a cyclic quadrilateral (four points on a circle). Ptolemy used it to compute chord tables — essentially tables of sine values — which underpinned all ancient astronomy. The theorem was rediscovered and generalized many times: by Abu al-Wafa (10th c.), Regiomontanus (15th c.), and in the modern complex-number form by Feuerbach and Schur in the 19th century.

The complex-number formulation reveals the algebraic essence of the theorem. For points on the unit circle z_k = e^{iθ_k}, the Ptolemy equality |z_2-z_3||z_1-z_4| = |z_1-z_2||z_3-z_4| is equivalent to the complex equation (z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4) = t·(z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4) for a positive real t. The key factorization exp(iα)-exp(iβ) = 2i·sin((α-β)/2)·exp(i(α+β)/2) reduces this to a sine ratio. The condition t > 0 then forces the signs of four half-angle sines into one of exactly two compatible patterns, corresponding to CCW and CW cyclic order.

The converse direction (Ptolemy equality ⇒ cyclic order) is harder than the forward direction. PtolemysTheoremOQ01.lean proves CCW ⇒ Ptolemy equality by direct calculation, but the converse requires recovering the angular ordering from the algebraic condition t > 0. This file uses an 8-case sign analysis on the product sin((θ_1-θ_2)/2)·sin((θ_3-θ_4)/2) vs. sin((θ_2-θ_3)/2)·sin((θ_1-θ_4)/2), of which only 2 of 8 sign patterns are compatible with t > 0 and distinct angles. One sorry remains in the sine ratio derivation (t_eq_sine_ratio), marked as suitable for Aristotle proof search.
overview.problemStatement: Given that PtolemysTheoremOQ01.lean proves CCW order → Ptolemy equality, the open question is: does Ptolemy equality imply cyclic order? This file answers yes, providing the converse and completing the biconditional for unit-circle points.
overview.proofStrategy: The proof derives from the exponential difference factorization exp(iα)-exp(iβ) = 2I·sin((α-β)/2)·exp(i(α+β)/2). Substituting zₖ = exp(iθₖ) into the proportionality equation and canceling phase factors yields a sine ratio. Since t > 0, an 8-case sign analysis shows only two sign patterns are consistent with distinct angles.
keyInsights: The sign of sin((θᵢ-θⱼ)/2) directly encodes the ordering of θᵢ and θⱼ
The constraint t > 0 forces the product of four sines to be positive, restricting angle orderings to exactly CCW or CW cyclic position
Only 2 of 8 sign patterns for the four half-angle sines are compatible with all angles being distinct

The half-angle factorization exp(iα)-exp(iβ) = 2i·sin((α-β)/2)·exp(i(α+β)/2) transforms complex differences into sine products. Substituting for all four z_k and canceling the exp(i(θ_k+θ_j)/2) phase factors leaves only the sine ratio for t.

The 8-case sign analysis is forced by the structure of t > 0: since t = sin((θ_2-θ_3)/2)·sin((θ_1-θ_4)/2) / [sin((θ_1-θ_2)/2)·sin((θ_3-θ_4)/2)], each of the four sines is either positive or negative (corresponding to angle ordering). Of 2^4 = 16 sign combinations, only those giving t > 0 are valid, reducing to 2 cases: all four same sign (t=1>0, cyclic order) or two pairs of opposite sign (t=product/product with both fractions positive).

conclusion.summary: Ptolemy equality ↔ CCW or CW order for distinct unit-circle points (under non-degeneracy conditions). The converse direction is new; the forward direction combines the result of PtolemysTheoremOQ01.lean with ptolemy_equality_of_proportional.
openQuestions: Can the non-degeneracy hypotheses (hdenom ≠ 0, hnumer ≠ 0) be relaxed or shown to follow from distinctness?
Can the sorry in t_eq_sine_ratio (the sine ratio identity) be filled by field_simp/ring after ring_nf applied to the ht_eq equation with substituted hha factorizations?
conclusion.implications: Completes the formal Lean 4 proof that Ptolemy's equality characterizes cyclic quadrilaterals. Demonstrates that half-angle sine sign analysis is a viable substitute for inscribed angle theorem arguments in formal proofs.
